$comment: The architecture contract for the ploaness repository itself, which is a pnpm workspace rather than a Payload application. It shares every framework-neutral rule with what consumers receive and differs only in the layer map, which is the one genuinely project-shaped part. It is named `-repo` rather than `.dependency-cruiser.json` because that path is FORBIDDEN in a governed project: a consumer may not hold a local copy of this contract, and a file with that name here would read as a counterexample.

forbidden.name: not-to-dev-dep
forbidden.comment: Published source must not import a devDependency. A consumer installs the package without them, so the import would resolve here and fail there. The specs are exempt because they ARE the development-only half.

forbidden.name: governance-stays-pure
forbidden.comment: The governance package is the pure-rule floor: every rule is a function over strings that were already read, which is what makes it unit-testable without building a fixture repository. It must therefore depend on no other ploaness package and reach nothing that performs I/O. `node:zlib` is deliberately not on the list: inflating a PNG's IDAT stream is a computation over bytes the caller already handed in, and banning it would push a rule into the CLI to escape a ban rather than to gain an ability. A rule that needed a file to be READ is a rule that belongs in the CLI, or an argument that belongs in its signature.

forbidden.name: nothing-imports-the-cli
forbidden.comment: The CLI holds every read and every process the harness starts, and nothing beneath it imports it back. The `ploaness` meta package is not beneath it: it is the consumer-facing package that re-exports every entry point, so it sits above the CLI and is exempt. Phrased as 'anything else must not import the CLI' rather than by enumerating the packages underneath, so a NEW package is governed the moment it exists.
